text: But there is widespread consumer distrust, such as in areas of food labelling, source of raw materials, and whether the products are genuine.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Because of this, management consulting and auditing firms, such as PricewaterhouseCoopers in Singapore, has started exploring "trust audit" for selected food manufacturing and supply companies in Asia, including for large Chinese State Own Enterprises.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: In fact, Singapore has one of the highest standards in Asia outside Japan.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Three reasons: one, in selected areas, such as fresh vegetables, processed food, poultry, Singapore has gone beyond certifying food that comes to Singapore.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Singapore is even sending officers overseas to accredit the food supply chain across the world for these key areas.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Second, Singapore has adopted food standards similar to those of the EU.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Therefore, the Singapore Government has set up, I was told, a certification arm in Jilin.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Over time, I was told, this certification arm will stamp the "Approved by Singapore" mark on those products, and these products will be eligible for import to Singapore.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Therefore, there are ample opportunities for Singapore-based companies to offer "trust audit” services in food which can include advisory service, certification services and assurance services which include regular internal or external audit, and, lastly, forensic service.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: How can we create these trust audit opportunities?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: SFA can work hand in glove with the Singapore Food Manufacturing Association and our professional services industries so as to embed trust audit into the Food Service Industry Transformation Map.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: SFA can also drive industry-wide research, set the relevant standards, recommend legislation, create the relevant ecosystem and identify training requirements.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Singapore businesses which pass through all these processes safely can also get the "Approved by Singapore" mark.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: I also believe that the Agency can create more economic opportunities for Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: With that, I stand in support of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Singapore has limited land available for farming, and we have limited fishing grounds as well.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Our local farms can produce only a small amount of food that we eat, and we are heavily reliant on food sourced overseas.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It is, therefore, critical that we place a strong emphasis on ensuring the security and safety of our food.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It is vital for SFA to continue the good work of AVA by ensuring that we continue to have diverse and reliable sources of food imports to prevent a situation of food shortage due to changes in the political climate of other countries, disease outbreaks or climate change.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: While we were ranked first in the Global Food Security Index, we achieved this mainly due to the affordability of our food.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: How does the Ministry and SFA intend to improve the quality and safety of our food imports?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It is also important that we continue to grow our domestic food supply as a key strategy in securing our food security.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In October 2017, the Singapore Agro-Food Enterprises Federation (SAFEF) announced that it will work with AVA and the Institutes of Higher Learning to improve the local agricultural sector in four key areas: set standards, boost productivity, enhance manpower development and lower costs.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Last month, I visited the SG Farmers Market organised by SAFEF at Cairnhill Community Club.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I was heartened to see that many of the stalls were helmed by young passionate Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: These new generation farmers have introduced new technology and innovative processes into their farming operations to enhance both the quality and the yield of their produce.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I hope SFA can do more to support our local young farmers in adopting technological innovations in their farming operations.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I would also like to take this opportunity to encourage all Singaporeans to support our local farmers and buy local produce.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: With the creation of SFA and the powers accorded to it, there must be enhanced measures put in place to strengthen our food safety regime.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Under the current policy, food hygiene certificate holders only need to attend their first refresher training after five years from completing their Basic Food Hygiene Course.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Subsequent refresher training courses are required only every 10 years thereafter.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I am of the view that the duration between recertification should be shortened to send a strong message to the industry on the importance of keeping a high level of food hygiene standard at the workplace.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Apart from ensuring our working people in the F&B industry adhere to stringent food hygiene guidelines, we also need to ensure that our food sources are safe for consumption.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: According to NEA, the amount of food waste generated in Singapore has increased by about 40% over the past 10 years.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We must tackle the issue of food wastage.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I am heartened to note that bigger supermarket chains, such as the National Trades Union Congress' (NTUC) Fairprice, have started to take this issue seriously.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Fairprice now packages “ugly-looking” fruits and vegetables, which are just as nutritional, and sell them at discounted rates, rather than to simply dispose of them.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I believe more can be done in terms of public education, and I would like SFA to take on an active role in reducing food wastage.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Another way of reducing food wastage is to better match producers of excess food to recipients who need it.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Can SFA also play a matchmaker role to link charitable organisations with those who have excess food that can be donated on a timely basis?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Two months ago, we launched two community refrigerators in Pek Kio.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Working with SG Food Rescue and the local market stallholders, we distributed more than 300 kg of fresh fruits and vegetables to more than 200 households at the launch event itself.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Since then, many more fruits and vegetables were donated and contributed.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I hope that SFA can work closer with social enterprises, such as SG Food Rescue and the Food Bank, to enhance community efforts to redistribute unwanted but edible food to those in need.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The Government needs to work with multiple stakeholders to monitor, educate and encourage safer and more responsible food production, food preparation and food consumption.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Over the years, a number of my Parliamentary seniors and colleagues had suggested this and I am very glad that we have finally managed to do so.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Climate change has resulted in more extreme weather patterns, affecting crop growth and harvests.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Overfishing and over-consumption of meat are taking their toll on our food ecosystem, and international research has found that humans’ increasing consumption of meat and dairy products is unsustainable.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Measures can include a combination of school and public education, subsidies for plant-based food and even lower rentals at food centres managed by the Agency.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Against this backdrop, we must continue to diversify our food sources and strengthen our ability to substitute various food items in the event of natural disasters or plant or animal disease outbreaks occurring at our usual food supply bases.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Singaporeans must be introduced to alternative foods, such as liquid egg products, and learn to adapt to the taste and cooking methods of a variety of such foods.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: A spate of food safety incidents last year reminds us of the importance of staying ever vigilant in our guard against lapses in the food sector.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Last but not least, we need to ensure free and rules-based maritime and air space navigation for transportation to ensure food supply security.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The SFA Bill is a concrete step in achieving that.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: My speech will touch on three points: food security, food safety and nutrition.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: My first point: self-sufficiency is important to Singapore.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Singapore has diversified our water resources to ensure that we are self-sufficient.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Food security is an important next step towards further self-sufficiency.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Singapore imports most of our food from our immediate neighbours.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: We have to import widely and diversely to minimise disruption to our food supplies.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Singapore aims to be friendly with our neighbours, but that is not always possible.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Food security is also necessary for affordable food costs.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: If we are unable to secure food sources easily, food prices will certainly rise.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In this aspect, SFA is instrumental in ensuring that Singaporeans can enjoy affordable food.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Can the Minister elaborate on how the Bill aims to manage such risks?

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: We have Temasek rice, high-tech fish farms, high-tech vegetable farms, to name a few, all started and operated by local companies.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Where there is an abundance of land, water, labour and, as the Minister mentioned, energy, this will help Singapore to further augment and secure our food supply.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Does SFA have any plans to implement farm-to-fork in overseas farms and fisheries where we source our food?

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: What can SFA do in conjunction with MTI to give more support to these local companies?

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Food security is not just about securing safe food sources.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It is also about having access to nutritious and healthy food.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: How will SFA ensure that Singaporeans have access to nutritious and healthy food?

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Does SFA have any plans to prevent the entry of unhealthy food into Singapore?

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Recent incidents of mass food poisoning have caused concern among Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: These incidents took place in various locations and settings, affecting Singaporeans from all walks of life, including children.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I have a resident in my ward who lost his hearing after eating raw fish.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: He used to be a high-level executive earning a good living taking care of his family.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: But now, he has lost his job, he cannot work and his family had to make serious adjustments to their lives.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Nevertheless, public trust in Singapore’s food safety remains strong.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Our strong track record and robust regulations play a part in this.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Yet, we are only as strong as the weakest link.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In one of the food poisoning incidents, it was found that food was handled and managed in an unsanitary manner.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Something that is so basic and yet not done properly.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: How would SFA intend to strengthen regulation and oversight of food safety?

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Oversight and enforcement are likely to be challenges for SFA and related agencies.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Dangerous and harmful food products are threats to public health.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Another example is the 2008 milk scandal in China which led to the stockpiling of milk powder.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Affordable safe food is, therefore, not a luxury but a public good that everyone should have access to.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: An agency which helps to make food safer and readily available plays an important role in ensuring that we keep our national identity.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: (In Malay):  : Some time ago, we faced issues on several matters related to national security.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Just to name two: one is the issue of oil supply and the other is water.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Over the years, through good strategic planning, we were able to navigate ourselves so that we are able to build ample reserves of these two resources to meet our national security needs.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Today, we are addressing another one of these challenges and that is food safety and supply.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We have seen how, in recent years, food safety and supply are in the limelight.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: There was the outbreak of bovine spongiform encephalopathy or “mad cow”, and then the avian influenza which undermined consumer confidence in the producers as well as the processors, and even in the governments where these diseases broke out.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We can see how, during the festive season, from Chinese New Year, Hari Raya to Deepavali, certain food items would experience a spike in prices.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Sometimes, this is because supply is temporarily disrupted due to disease outbreak and, at other times, it was because of supply-demand factors.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Therefore, NTUC Fairprice and other importers, with the support from our Government, have, in recent times, been actively looking at alternative sources of supply.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This is important so that we could be assured of a stable supply.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Can I ask the Minister how are we tapping on our business organisations to continually look for new and reliable sources of supply?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Is there a need for SFA to tap on bodies like EDB or even our Trade Consular Officers under MFA to source for new food supply?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In key strategic countries, would there be a need for SFA to set up its own offices in these countries, so that we can get our man on the ground to look at the production, processing and handling as well as testing before the food reaches our shores?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We are also living in an age where production and farming overseas will have artificial preservatives added to foods.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: For example, the preservatives used to stop the browning and discoloration of food have been linked to an asthma-related sensitivity and allergy in some cases.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: How do we then monitor the use of artificial preservatives in food products that are imported here?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Some of these synthetic preservatives are harmful to health.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: For example, last October, the US FDA removed seven synthetic flavouring substances and flavour enhancers from its list of approved food additives.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Based on evidence presented to FDA by the various petitioners, who stated that benzophenone causes cancer in animals, the FDA amended the food additive regulations to no longer provide for its use as a plasticiser in rubber articles intended for repeated use in contact with food.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: A restaurant, for example, that may not own the premises, but is merely a tenant?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Another issue which I would like to ask is whether there any process for an owner or management of a restaurant to ensure that all its employees who are handling food are in good health.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Would a restaurant be penalised if, say, its employee has a bad flu and yet he is in the kitchen handling food?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: As we know, prevention is better than reacting and suspending a food establishment only after people fall victim to food poisoning.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Therefore, the scope of the new Agency is very wide and it would require a large team to check the food industry, from manufacturing right down to the kitchen in restaurants and other places where food is served to customers.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: With that, Mr Speaker, I support this Bill.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: SFA will focus on food safety and food security.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Food safety is a prerequisite for a resilient food supply, and key to developing a thriving agri-food industry.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Allow me to outline SFA’s priorities in these two areas and address some of the specific comments.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Ong Teng Koon referred to recent potential disruptions in our egg and seafood imports and asked how SFA can better handle such incidents without causing alarm.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The answer is that SFA will ensure our food security by developing and enhancing our three national strategies to obtain food.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: First, SFA will build on the existing work by AVA to diversify import sources.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We take for granted apples from Poland, bananas from Ecuador and Mandarin oranges from China in our supermarkets.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: These are, in fact, the fruits of a deliberate strategy to diversify our food sources.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Imports will remain our largest food basket for the foreseeable future.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: SFA, in partnership with relevant Government agencies like MFA and Enterprise Singapore (ESG), will continue to diversify our food sources, as Er Dr Lee Bee Wah, Mr Melvin Yong and Mr Saktiandi Supaat have suggested.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This includes working with importers to organise overseas sourcing trips and business matching sessions, as well as increasing the number of farms across different countries which can export to Singapore.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In fact, our officers were accrediting farms in Thailand over the Lunar New Year break while many of us Singaporeans were taking a break and enjoying good food with our families.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Our food importers are also a key node in the supply chain, and we must ensure that they are prepared to withstand potential shocks from climate change and geopolitical developments, as highlighted by Mr Mohamed Irshad.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As Mr Ong Teng Koon has highlighted, food security is fundamental to national security.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In the long run, securing our food supply is also the primary way to mitigate price volatility and spikes.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This is a focus of SFA, which will continue to contribute to whole-of-Government efforts to provide affordable food accessible to all Singaporeans, as highlighted by Assoc Prof Daniel Goh.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Second, SFA will intensify efforts to grow an agri-food ecosystem in Singapore, as suggested by Mr Mohamed Irshad and Mr Melvin Yong, thereby reducing our dependence on imports.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This requires close coordination between SFA and other Government agencies in domains, such as land planning, industry development and financing, and skills training.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: SFA will also partner our industry stakeholders across the food supply chain to catalyse industry transformation.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Transforming the industry requires us to cultivate a generation of "agri-specialists".

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: AVA has been working with our Institutes of Higher Learning in this area.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: One such initiative is the "Earn and Learn Programme", a work-study programme through which students from Temasek Polytechnic and Republic Polytechnic work at local farms and apply the knowledge and practical skills learnt in school.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: SFA will continue working with the industry and the Institutes of Higher Learning to enhance manpower development for the agriculture sector, as raised by Mr Melvin Yong, and create meaningful value-added jobs for our future workforce.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Given our lack of natural resources, such as land and water, the future of farming in Singapore has to be one that is technology- and R&D-driven, climate-resilient and resource-efficient with high productivity.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We recognise the contributions by our existing farmers.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: They bring valuable experience and we would like to continue working with them to improve Singapore’s food security.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will take a pragmatic approach by helping existing farms modernise.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In addition to productivity, we will also prioritise the environmental sustainability of food production.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As part of the MEWR family, SFA will work closely with NEA and the Public Utilities Board to find synergies in food production, water, waste and energy.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This will ensure that our local food supply will remain resilient in the face of wider trends, such as resource scarcity and climate change.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Together, we can become a world leader in agri-food solutions, just like how we have turned our constraints in water to strategic advantages.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Our Water Story, which Members, including Er Dr Lee Bee Wah and Ms Anthea Ong, had talked about, is well-known internationally.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: SFA will work together across the Government, and with industry and other stakeholders, including fellow Singaporeans, to write the Singapore Food Story.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Third, SFA will continue supporting our companies to expand and grow overseas.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Henry Kwek has also rightly identified this as an area of tremendous economic opportunity for our local companies, especially if our companies develop expertise in highly sought-after farming technologies that are resource-efficient, high-yield, and climate-resilient.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I hope to see more of our local farms succeeding in overseas markets.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Our three food baskets are what I call "supply-side strategies".

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: However, the demand side of the equation is equally important.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: SFA will continue to prioritise public education and outreach to complement the three food baskets, as mentioned by Mr Mohamed Irshad.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: These include supporting local produce, as suggested by Er Dr Lee Bee Wah and Mr Melvin Yong, and promoting the consumption of substitutes, such as liquid eggs and more sustainable foods, such as plant-based protein, as suggested by Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Mr Mohamed Irshad.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I would also like to assure Mr Saktiandi Supaat that even as we allow new food to come in, SFA will take reference from global standards, such as those set by the Codex Alimentarius Commission, in permitting food additives for use in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Ms Anthea Ong and Mr Melvin Yong raised an important initiative which AVA and NEA are already collaborating on – reducing food waste.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In fact, food waste is one of NEA's priorities in the Year Towards Zero Waste.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: My Ministry recognises that Government regulations may promote the reduction of food waste, and will look further into it with our partners, taking into consideration other factors, such as food safety and business costs.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I urge Ms Anthea Ong, Mr Melvin Yong and other Members to continue supporting community efforts to redistribute food better so that there is no hunger even among our needy and, in the process, reduce food waste.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I will now move on to outline three strategies which SFA will adopt to ensure the safety of food in Singapore, an area which many Members have spoken about.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: These range from providing a single contact point for the public to provide feedback, as suggested by Ms Anthea Ong, to combining contact tracing and industry engagement operations.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This will allow SFA to manage more holistically across the entire farm-to-fork supply chain to pinpoint and remedy critical points, and react more quickly to food safety incidents, as raised by Er Dr Lee Bee Wah, Prof Fatimah Lateef and Mr Saktiandi Supaat.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: These efforts over the years have strengthened coordination across the Government in response to food safety threats.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: AVA, NEA and the Ministry of Health (MOH) work closely under the One Health framework and follow a protocol to respond to and address food-borne outbreaks.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Information received by each agency, whether from individuals or doctors and laboratories, is tracked and analysed centrally to ensure that any unusual increase in notifications linked to food establishments is investigated promptly.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Second, having a single agency like the SFA will support consistent administration and enforcement of the regulatory framework for food establishments, balanced against supporting enterprise and job creation.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As Er Dr Lee Bee Wah, Mr Mohamed Irshad and Ms Anthea Ong have suggested, we can harness technology and data to make our regulatory regime more effective and efficient.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Joyvio, one of the largest end-to-end fruit companies in China, developed an app that tracks the product's thousand-mile journey from a vine to the supermarket shelf.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: With a simple scan, shoppers can tell which field the fruit came from, who was in charge of its production, what tests it went through before entering the market, and even details about the soil and water tests from the farm.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This allows consumers to check that the fruit has not been contaminated anywhere along the way.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As suggested by Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Mr Saktiandi Supaat, SFA will also raise the level of accountability of operators and the food industry which must take greater responsibility for the hygiene standards at their premises to ensure food safety.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This will be complemented with robust enforcement, as suggested by Mr Leon Perera.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Where necessary, we will enhance regulatory oversight and penalties.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As Mr Mohamed Irshad has highlighted, our regulatory regime will need to evolve with changing business models, including online food sales and food delivery.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Our vision is for businesses across the supply chain to only have to interface with one agency.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This will take time, and we will work closely with the industry to put in place facilitative regulations.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For example, we are looking into ways to streamline the licences for premises carrying out both central kitchen and catering operations.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As pointed out by Mr Henry Kwek, there is much potential to leverage the trusted food safety standards in Singapore to promote internationalisation efforts by the food industry.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This is an area that SFA will continue to work with MTI and ESG on.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Mohamed Irshad has suggested that SFA could tap on similar opportunities in the halal food market.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: MUIS will primarily focus on certification of halal food for consumption by Muslims in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: SFA will support our food companies to look for opportunities in the region and the Middle East.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Ong Teng Koon and Prof Fatimah Lateef asked about the role of SFA with regard to nutrition.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: HPB will continue to promote the consumption of healthy food, and SFA will provide the relevant support.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Leon Perera spoke about food labelling as a tool to help consumers make informed choices.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: AVA already imposes regulations to provide consumers with pertinent information, such as ingredients and allergens.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: SFA will continue to work with partner agencies, such as MOH and HPB, on food labelling.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Third, forming a single agency like SFA will enable deepening of food safety expertise in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This further ensures that our food continues to be safe for consumption, and standards are benchmarked internationally.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: NCFS will also develop commercial laboratories to support the food safety testing needs of food businesses as production and exports increase.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: SFA will draw on the lessons learnt and results achieved by AVA, NEA and HSA, and write a new chapter in the Singapore Food Story by bringing together stakeholders from farm-to-fork to co-create solutions to ensure and secure a supply of safe food for our people.
